New Delhi, October 15: Reiterating India’s stand on cross-border terrorism, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Thursday asserted that any further terrorist acts originating from Pakistan would invite an even stronger response.
He emphasised that while India’s cultural ethos favoured dialogue, coexistence and peaceful resolution of disputes, its commitment to peace should not be mistaken for weakness.

“Operation Sindoor, Balakot Airstrikes and Surgical Strikes weren’t just military operations; they symbolised a decisive shift in the nation’s approach, moving from diplomatic condemnation to proactive action aimed at rooting out terrorism by reaching its very source,” Singh said at the Times Network Defence Conclave in New Delhi.

Defence Minister termed strength and capability as essential to maintaining peace, and underlined that India hopes for peace, but remains prepared for war that sometimes becomes necessary to protect the nation.
“Our commitment to peace remains steadfast, yet we are fully prepared to confront any challenge.

Our goal is to build an India that, while advocating for peace, remains vigilant when it comes to security and is fully capable of safeguarding its sovereignty, integrity, and national interests,” he said.
On the evolving security landscape, Singh underscored the need for heightened vigilance and preparedness in an era of hybrid, high-tech and hyper warfare.

He highlighted the growing complexity of security threats in the digital age, identifying what he described as the ‘5D Security Threat ’-Disinformation, Destabilisation, Disruption, Deception and Destruction.

He pointed out that terrorism was evolving beyond organised groups, and emerging threats include ‘lone-wolf’ attacks and ‘white-collar terrorism’, which make it increasingly difficult for security agencies to identify radicalised individuals and prevent potential attacks.

The Defence Minister referred to the recent incident involving a co-pilot who allegedly attempted to crash a passenger aircraft and Captain Smit Machhar who risked his life to avert a major terror attack.
“The incident underscored the threat posed by lone-wolf attackers while demonstrating how the courage and commitment of an individual could thwart the designs of those driven by hatred.
A single alert and courageous individual could help foil an entire terrorist plot.
On defence preparedness, Singh underscored the need to combine ‘hard power’ with ‘soft power’ and called for a shift towards ‘smart power’.

“Modern defence strategies must integrate precision-guided weapons and loitering munitions with cost-effective weaponry, human intelligence with artificial intelligence, and advanced systems with low-cost, agile and adaptable technologies to address evolving security challenges,” he said.

On the growth witnessed by the defence sector due to the Government’s efforts, Singh stated that defence production has risen to a record over Rs 1.78 lakh crore from Rs 40,000 crore in 2014, with defence exports touching an all-time high of Rs 39,000 crore from Rs 686 crore in 2013-14, and India defence products reaching nearly 100 countries.

He exuded confidence that the nation would achieve defence production targets of Rs 2 lakh crore this year and Rs 3 lakh crore by 2029, and export defence equipment worth Rs 50,000 crore by 2029, the Ministry said in its statement.

The Defence Minister attributed the growth to reforms that simplified export procedures, including the introduction of the Defence EXIM Portal, online approvals, the Open General Export License, streamlined quality certification and the ‘Green Channel’ policy.
These measures, he said, enhanced India’s global credibility and prepared domestic industries to compete in international markets.

"The Ministry of Defence has approved procurement of goods and services worth over Rs 2,400 crore from start-ups and MSMEs and sanctioned projects exceeding Rs 1,500 crore for new technology development.
As of March 2026, iDEX had engaged 676 start-ups and innovators and facilitated the signing of 551 contracts.

From a few dozen defence startups in 2018, the ecosystem had grown to more than 2,000, with young enterprises working across drones, artificial intelligence, quantum technology, cybersecurity, robotics and other advanced fields,” he added.

Citing progress in ammunition manufacturing, he said 159 of the 175 ammunition variants used by the Defence Forces were now indigenously produced, representing more than 90 per cent self-reliance in ammunition variants.

Referring to India’s exports of bulletproof jackets to over 100 countries, he noted that the country was the fourth in the world to establish a national standard for bulletproof jackets aligned with international norms.
He also spoke about the implementation of the One Rank.
One Pension scheme and the creation of the Chief of Defence Staff post, terming them significant measures undertaken to strengthen the defence framework.

stories.title: Flood-affected Bihar man dies after being ‘hit by air-dropped relief material’
stories.summary: Officials in Saran district said a relief packet dropped from a helicopter allegedly struck the man’s head, though police said no injury marks were found on his body

article_sentences: A 58-year-old man died after allegedly being hit by relief material dropped from a helicopter in flood-hit Saran district of Bihar, officials said on Saturday (October 3, 2026).
The incident took place on Friday (October 2, 2026) afternoon near a relief camp in Parshurampur village, in the Amnour police station area.
The deceased was identified as Anil Kumar Singh, a resident of the same village.
Savindra Kumar Das, Sub-Divisional.
Police Officer (SDPO), Marhaura, said: "Prima facie, it appears that around 3.30 p.m. on Friday, a relief material packet dropped by a helicopter allegedly hit a man on his head, causing his death."
The body has been sent to a hospital for post-mortem, and the police are conducting further investigation, he added.
"The exact cause of death could be ascertained only after receiving the autopsy report," Mr. Das said.

Vimlesh Kumar, Station House Officer (SHO), Amnour police station, also cited villagers' allegation that the man died after being hit by the relief packet, but clarified that "no injury marks were found either on his head or other parts of the body."
Referring to another incident, Mr. Kumar said a low-flying helicopter had caused a tin shed to blow away and hit a woman on her leg, leading to a minor injury.
"She has been treated at a medical facility and is fine now," he added.

stories.summary: A major controversy erupted when T.N. Seshan went to court challenging the appointment of two Election Commissioners; N. Gopalaswami’s suo motu recommendation to the President for the removal of Navin Chawla was another shocking episode

article_sentences: The story so far: From Sukumar Sen's tenure, during which the first general election in India was held in 1951-52, to October 16, 1986, the Election Commission had only one member: the Chief Election Commissioner.
In S.S. Dhanoa.

Union of India (1991), the Supreme Court stressed that under Article 342(2) of the Constitution, the President could fix and appoint as many Election Commissioners as he may, from time to time, determine, though it was desirable to have a multi-member commission.

In October 1989, when the Rajiv Gandhi government was in power, the President notified the appointment of Mr. Dhanoa and V.S. Seigell as Election Commissioners to complete the team with Chief Election Commissioner R.V.S. Peri Sastry.

The premise was the increased workload in conducting the elections after the minimum voting age was lowered from 21 to 18, but political observers then saw it as a move by the government to hem Mr. Sastry in.

The multi-member arrangement was short-lived as the President revoked his 1989 notification after the new V.P. Singh government took over and was not in favour of the appointments made by the previous government.
Mr. Dhanoa went to court, which said it was the President’s discretion to determine the number of Election Commissioners.

In the current situation, when two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, have objected to the style of functioning of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, here is a look at the episodic disputes on the panel that have broken out in public.
On October 1, 1993, the President appointed M.S. Gill and G.V.G. Krishnamurthy as Election Commissioners.
Ever since, the commission has been a three-member body.

The President promulgated an Ordinance, later enacted as the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners (Condition of Service) Amendment Act, with retrospective effect from October 1, 1993.
The Act explicitly granted coordinate powers to the Election Commissioners, solving a grey area in the Constitution.

stories.headline: US teen held over alleged plot to attack Hindu place of worship
stories.title: US teen held over alleged plot to attack Hindu place of worship
stories.summary: New York, Oct 15 : A teenager was arrested for allegedly plotting to carry out a "mass shooting" at a Hindu place of worship in the US state of Illinois, with investigators recovering a manifesto expressing white supremacist ideology and references to violence against people of Indian descent. Alexandros Paporakis, 19, of Palatine village was arrested on October 11 and charged with making a terrorist threat and unlawful possession of a weapon. According to investigators, the youth had tried to open fire "potentially targeting" the place of worship in the Aurora city in Illinois, but his gun jammed, forcing him to drive back home, a move that prevented a mass murder. The specific intended location has not been disclosed by the authorities. Palatine Police detectives examined electronic communications and a document attributed to Paporakis titled "Why I Fought: A.K.A.: (Aurora Shooter's Manifesto)", which contained "statements expressing white supremacist and extremist ideologies, including references to violence directed toward individuals of South Asian heritage, particularly those of Indian descent". Detectives believe Paporakis may have been planning to carry out the attack on October 11. "However, the specific intended location has not been confirmed and remains under investigation," police said on Wednesday. The Consulate General of India in Chicago said it appreciated the timely action by law enforcement authorities and was in touch with members of the Indian diaspora while closely monitoring developments. The arrest comes amid celebrations of Hindu festivals, including Navaratri and Durga Puja, and just two weeks after the Shree Swaminarayan Vadtal Dham Hindu Mandir in Richmond Heights, Ohio, was vandalised. On October 11, the Palatine Police Department was contacted by the Mount Prospect Police Department regarding information it had received about a potential mass shooting. The information originated from an individual who reported receiving concerning electronic communications from Paporakis. According to a report by NBC Chicago, Paporakis had worked as a cashier at fast-food restaurant Taco Bell and had plotted to carry out a "mass shooting of Indian people" at a Hindu temple in Aurora. He drove to the temple last Sunday "decked out for war". The day he chose to carry out the carnage at the sprawling place of worship was filled with people. He was "one malfunctioning rifle away from becoming a mass shooter". Paporakis showed up "to kill a significant number of Indians", the report said, quoting police. Investigators said he had a "modified AR-style rifle and 300 rounds of ammo, enough to fill ten magazines for reloading, along with body armour, gasoline cans" and an assortment of Hakenkreuz (hooked cross used by Nazis), the report said. Paporakis allegedly drove from his mother's home in Palatine to the Aurora temple. Authorities said that "he tried to open fire but the gun jammed, so he drove home". There he "searched the internet trying to learn how to unjam his gun and called a colleague, informing them of (his) intent to carry out a mass shooting". The co-worker then notified the police, informing them of the plot, and Paporakis was arrested Sunday before he could return to the temple. The youth was arrested as he was leaving his residence following a coordinated response by the Palatine and Mount Prospect police departments. Paporakis has been charged with one count of making a terrorist threat and one count of unlawful possession of weapons. He appeared for a detention hearing on Wednesday at the Cook County Third Municipal District Courthouse in Rolling Meadows, where a judge ordered him detained. His next court appearance is scheduled for October 30. According to investigators, Paporakis "expressed pleasure calling himself a sociopathic white supremacist Neo-Nazi filled with hatred, fantasising about mass murder nearly every day". In a social media post, the Hindu American Foundation commended law enforcement for swift action. "We also urge the community to stay vigilant and report any potential threat. Every community deserves to worship without fear," it said. The Coalition of Hindus of North America (CoHNA) said the "disturbing plot" comes as Hindus gather in large numbers to celebrate Navratri, and just two weeks after an attack on a temple in Ohio. "Hindu temples and all houses of worship must be sanctuaries of peace, prayer, and solace - NEVER targets of hate, violence, or terror. We thank law enforcement for their swift action in averting what could have been an unspeakable tragedy. "We urge elected officials and law enforcement agencies to take the growing threats against Hindu places of worship seriously, strengthen protections, and unequivocally condemn Hinduphobia," it said in a social media post. The group called on temples and community organisations to review their security measures, remain vigilant, and promptly report suspicious activity. "The freedom to worship without fear is a fundamental American right. It must be protected," it said. Police said they were working with the FBI as the investigation continued, including a review of possible additional charges. Authorities have not identified any known ongoing threat to the public associated with the incident. "The seriousness of this alleged threat cannot be overstated... Protecting our communities and places of worship remains a priority," Palatine Police Chief William Nord said. FBI Chicago Special Agent in Charge Ryan Whalen said the agency aggressively works alongside its local and state law enforcement partners to identify, investigate, and dismantle any threats of violence driven by radical ideologies. stories.title: India’s merchandise exports climb 23% to $44.4 bn in September
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 15 : India's merchandise exports recorded a robust 23.04 per cent growth year-on-year to touch a four-month high of $44.4 billion in September this year, despite the uncertainties in global markets and the disruption in shipping due to the escalating Middle East conflict, official figures released on Thursday showed. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agarwal said the growth trend in India's exports was continuing, indicating sustained momentum in outbound shipments. The growth in goods exports was driven by a broad-based increase in shipments across sectors, with particularly strong growth in petroleum products, meat, dairy and poultry products, handicrafts, and some cereals, he added. Imports rose 8 per cent to $74.61 billion during the month due to the increase in prices of crude oil in the global market. The surge in exports also led to a narrowing of the trade deficit to $30.21 billion during the month on a year-on-year basis from around $33 billion recorded in September 2025. However, on a sequential basis, the trade deficit was higher than the corresponding figure of $26.86 billion in the previous month of August. Cumulatively, goods exports stood at $259.89 billion during April-September, up nearly 19 per cent year-on-year. Imports rose 16 per cent year-on-year to $437.53 billion in the first six months of financial year 2026-27 (FY27). As a result, the merchandise trade deficit stood at $177.64 billion during the six-month period. Strong growth in merchandise exports has also increased their contribution to gross domestic product (GDP), after the share of exports recorded a consistent decline over the past three financial years. Exports accounted for 14 per cent of GDP in the first quarter of FY27, the latest figures show. Following a slowdown in global demand in FY24 and FY25, and the uncertainties triggered by the US tariff turmoil in FY26, the share of exports in GDP declined to 11.3 per cent in FY26 from 11.7 per cent in FY25. --IANS

article_sentences: In a setback to private lender Yes Bank, the Supreme Court on Thursday upheld the Bombay High Court’s judgment quashing the bank’s ₹8,415 crore AT-1 bond write-off.
The verdict has implications for how banks use these instruments to absorb losses during a financial crisis and for investors who hold them.
It could clarify the extent to which banks can write off these instruments during a financial crisis and the legal procedures they must follow.

A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Augustine George Masih delivered its verdict after reserving judgment on 20 May, following submissions from the Centre, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Yes Bank, bondholders represented by Axis Trustee Services and other investors.
Before reserving judgment, the bench had sought Cabinet records connected with the reconstruction process, including resolutions, meeting minutes and related documents.
It had also sought details of the rules governing the relevant Cabinet meeting, quorum requirements and the names of members present when the decision was taken.
The dispute centres on whether Yes Bank’s administrator had the legal authority to cancel the bonds as part of the bank’s reconstruction plan, leaving investors with losses on their investments.
Additional Tier-1 (AT-1) bonds are financial instruments banks use to raise capital and strengthen their balance sheets.
Introduced under global banking reforms following the 2008 financial crisis, they have no fixed maturity date.
Investors generally receive interest, but the bonds carry higher risks than ordinary debt instruments.
Under specified conditions, they can be written off or converted into shares to absorb losses when a bank faces financial distress.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court has held that a person having parted with his share in a property via a compromise deed cannot later execute a gift deed in relation to the same property.

The Court faulted the Telangana High Court's order for overlooking a compromise deed before upholding the execution of a gift deed by a man who had already relinquished his share via a compromise deed.

A bench of Justice Sanjay Kumar and Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva heard a case in which a man, despite having relinquished his claim over properties allotted to his mother under a 1986 compromise in exchange for absolute rights over a house property, subsequently executed a gift deed in 2007 in respect of the same properties.

The core legal issue before the Court was whether a gift deed could be upheld without properly appreciating the effect of an earlier family settlement and a compromise decree that had recognised the parties' respective rights over the properties.
The dispute arose from a family settlement executed on April 19, 1959, dividing ancestral properties among family members.
Under the settlement, Madhusudhan Reddy received specific properties, while certain lands in Karkalpahad village were allotted to his mother, Manikyamma.
Subsequently, during the pendency of litigation concerning the family properties, Madhusudhan Reddy entered into a compromise with Anasuyamma and her adopted son, Venkatraji Reddy, in February 1986.
Under the settlement, he relinquished his claim over the properties allotted to his mother and secured absolute rights over the Himayatnagar house.
The compromise was recorded by the High Court, which allowed the appeal in terms of the settlement in September 1990.
However, in April 2007, Madhusudhan Reddy executed a registered gift deed in favour of Siddhartha Reddy, transferring several parcels of land in Karkalpahad village.

The appellants contended that the lands covered by the deed had not been allotted to Madhusudhan Reddy under the 1959 family settlement and were among the properties over which he had relinquished his claims under the 1986 compromise.

Anasuyamma, Venkatraji Reddy and another family member subsequently filed a suit seeking a declaration of title, a declaration that the gift deed was null and void, mutation of revenue records and a permanent injunction.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court has criticised the manner in which the Allahabad High Court has dealt with a case while granting probation to two men convicted for a brutal attack that left a victim with grievous injuries.
The Court said that the accused were released on probation in ignorance of the adverse report submitted by the probation officer against them.
“The High Court, despite the overwhelming adverse report on the 'character of the offenders' and giving short shrift to the 'nature of the offence', released the accused on good conduct.

The High Court upheld the conviction but extended the benefit of Section 4 of the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 (“PoO Act”), directing the accused to execute personal bonds of ₹20,000 each and maintain peace and good behaviour for one year.

stories.title: Supreme Court Quashes Rajasthan High Court's Disciplinary Proceedings Against Judge Over Bail Order
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has quashed disciplinary proceedings initiated against a Rajasthan judicial officer(since retired) for granting bail to two accused persons despite their earlier bail applications having been rejected by the High Court, observing that counselling or a warning would have sufficed in the peculiar facts of the case.

A bench of Justice B.V. Nagarathna, Justice R. Mahadevan and Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya directed the Rajasthan Government and the High Court to recompute the officer's pay under the revised pay scale and release his terminal benefits, including pension and arrears, within three months, subject to there being no other legal impediment.
The case concerned Mukesh Tyagi, who was serving as a Special Judge under the POCSO Act at Dholpur when he granted bail to two accused persons in May 2019.
The Rajasthan High Court subsequently cancelled the bail, observing that no change in circumstances had occurred after the accused persons' earlier bail applications were rejected.

Following the High Court's direction to place its order before the Chief Justice, disciplinary proceedings were initiated against the petitioner-judicial officer under Rule 16 of the Rajasthan Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1958, alleging gross judicial impropriety and indiscipline, following which the petitioner moved the Supreme Court.
The Supreme Court declined to interfere with the High Court's observations but separately held that the disciplinary inquiry was unwarranted in the circumstances.
“…in the facts and circumstances of this case, the initiation of an inquiry was not at all required.
Possibly the entry of the remarks of the learned Single Judge in the Annual Confidential Report (ACR) would have sufficed.

We have also stated, the petitioner/judicial officer could have been counseled and warned to be more careful in future and to give sufficient weightage to the orders of the High Court particularly when the same were passed earlier in the same case by the High Court.

In the circumstance, we find that the Memorandum dated 25.10.2024 at Annexure P-6, the statement of charges under Rule 16 of the Rules, the allegation of charge etc. were not warranted for in the instant case.”, the Court held.
The Court also noted that the petitioner's Annual Confidential Reports were positive and that he had retired on March 31, 2026, while his revised pay and terminal benefits remained unreleased.
Accordingly, the Court quashed the disciplinary memorandum dated October 25, 2024, and the related charges.
